title: Model-flavor selection inversion caused sticky warm-cache and cross-region routing churn
creator: Lina Park
description: Summary: During a regional capacity pressure event on 2026-02-28 we observed sustained traffic churn across three regions and elevated error rates for hosted customers using routing policies with tiered model flavors. Root cause analysis shows a policy-weight inversion combined with an edge warm-cache sticky behavior: routing policy updates propagated asynchronously and were applied out-of-order by the router fleet, which temporarily promoted a low-cost model-flavor (quant-reduced) into the ‘preferred’ slot. That model-flavor’s runtime characteristics caused increased latency and frequent KV cache misses, which triggered automated capacity escalations and cross-region reroutes. The reroutes propagated back to the policy controller and created repeated churn for ~45 minutes before mitigation.
impact_details:
- Affected customers: ~120 hosted API keys spanning small/medium customers; top 10 affected customers saw 3–8x latency increases and elevated 5xx rates for 35 minutes.
- Platform: per-token cost increased due to repeated cold KV cache warms and inefficient batching; autoscaler spun up GPUs in secondary regions leading to short-term cost spike.
- SLOs: p50 latency breached by 60%, p95 by 210% in the impacted region window.
timeline: 2026-02-28T09:42Z - Alert: multi-region latency and 5xx spike triggered from routing telemetry (pager)
2026-02-28T09:47Z - On-call routing & runtime teams paged; mitigation: temporary traffic pin to primary region for impacted customers
2026-02-28T09:54Z - Identified out-of-order policy application in router logs and sticky warm-cache hits dropping sharply
2026-02-28T10:05Z - Emergency rollback of recent routing policy push (release routing-2.5.0) to restore previous policy ordering
2026-02-28T10:30Z - Traffic stabilized but telemetry showed continued oscillation in a small subset of router instances; started targeted instance restart
2026-02-28T10:55Z - Full stabilization confirmed at 10:55Z; incident declared resolved at 11:10Z after 30-minute observation window
root_cause_analysis: Policy controller publishes tiered-weight updates as a series of delta messages; routers subsribe and apply in best-effort order. Under load the message queue delivered updates out-of-order due to a rare requeue path introduced in 2025-11 that re-prioritizes older messages if backpressure observed.

A recent optimization (ENG-70412) changed model-flavor preference calculation to prefer lower-cost flavors aggressively; combined with out-of-order delivery this resulted in a transient inversion where a quant-reduced flavor replaced the high-recall flavor for a set of customer routes.

Routers maintain an LRU-like warm-cache affinity for KV prefix entries; when a new flavor replaced the expected model, the cache warmed poorly for initial requests causing higher tail latency and more CPU/GPU load which in turn triggered autoscaler heuristics and cross-region failovers.
Telemetry and traces show a feedback loop: cache misses -> increased latency -> capacity probe -> reroute -> new region experiences the same out-of-order policy application -> repeat.
Lack of end-to-end ordering guarantees and insufficient per-policy sequencing metadata made detection and safe reconciliation slow during the incident.
short_term_mitigations_completed: Rolled back routing controller commit that introduced requeue prioritization (release routing-2.5.0 rollback).
Pinned affected customer traffic to origin region for 45 minutes to break the feedback loop.
Restarted 6 router instances with stale policy state to ensure fresh policy pulls.
Added a temporary circuit-breaker to prevent immediate autoscaler-triggering from repeated cache-miss-driven probes (config change).
long_term_action_items: (Owner: Arjun) Add monotonic sequence numbers to policy updates and enforce apply-order at router-side; design doc in progress: https://confluence.redwood.ai/routing/seq-numbers (due 2026-03-08).
(Owner: Priya S.) Rework the message queue requeue path to avoid prioritizing older deltas during backpressure; PR linked: https://github.com/redwoodinc/routing/pull/1142 (in review).
(Owner: Runtime) Implement model-flavor warm-cache compatibility checks before swap: routers should validate KV-prefix hit-rate threshold before accepting a flavor transition for hot routes.
(Owner: SRE) Update autoscaler heuristics to ignore short-lived latency spikes caused by cache warm events; add a 30s dampening window to probes.
(Owner: DX) Create a runbook for policy-order anomalies that includes a single-command reconcile and a dashboard widget that surfaces sequence gaps.
(Owner: PM) Coordinate a staged rollout plan for routing-2.5.1 with canaries and policy-seq verification for 2 weeks in low-traffic regions before global rollout.
current_work_and_notes: Sequence-number design doc circulating with feedback from runtime and routing teams; concern raised about additional storage overhead for per-policy sequence metadata — exploring delta-compression approach.
Message queue fix landed in branch but failing one flakiness test; testing with longer soak in staging (SRE: +48h).
Prototype of warm-cache validation available in runtime dev branch; microbenchmarks show ~18% reduction in cold-start CPU when validating prefix compatibility.
Eng review feedback (Lina): ensure rollbacks are safe and that sequence fallback path tolerates dropped messages (proposal: fetch latest full snapshot if sequence gap > 3).
Security review: no customer data exfiltration; KMS usage unchanged. Marked security_review_required=false.
review_comments: PM review (Janelle): prioritize runbook and dashboard widget before the full rollout — we need automated alerting to detect sequence gaps early.
Design review (Marco): warm-cache validation must avoid false negatives for legitimate flavor swaps; propose metric-based gating rather than binary check.
SRE review (Keon): agree with 30s dampening but recommend separate threshold for p95 vs p50 probes to avoid masking real platform regressions.

acceptance_criteria: Routers apply policy updates in sequence order 100% of the time in staging for 72h soak with no observed gaps.
Warm-cache validation prevents >80% of flavor-induced cold starts in the canary region during 2-week canary.
Dashboard shows sequence gaps as an actionable alert and runbook reduces mean-time-to-reconcile to <5 minutes.
Autoscaler dampening reduces repeated cross-region escalations in synthetic tests by >90%.
Routing-2.5.1 rollout completed to production with canary verification and post-deploy checks passed.
